name: Hai Tang Pagoda
kicker: Pagoda above the fields called Đồng Chùa
summary: Pagoda in Bai Lang: walk up from the landing for a short stop at the gate, the statue, and Đồng Chùa. It faces the terraced fields, with the hill behind the gate. The first building dates to 1758 and the move to 1848, after storm damage. Leave time for the boat back.
timeNeeded: A short walk from the landing
getThere: Walk through Bai Lang after the boat.
heroCaption: The gate, the Quan Âm, and the hill behind Hải Tạng
body: Hải Tạng stands in Xóm Cấm, Bai Lang, on Hòn Lao. It faces southwest onto the fields called Đồng Chùa, with the hill behind it. You walk there from the landing.

The city page dates the first building to Cảnh Hưng 19 (1758), about 200 metres northeast of today’s site, and the move to Tự Đức 1 (1848) after storm damage. It also describes a 2002 repair of the main hall, a stone enclosure, a lotus pond, and a 3.5 metre plaster Quan Âm in front of the three-door gate. Read 1758 and 1848 as two dates: the first building, then the move after storm damage. National relic, 2006.

The heritage pages describe the yin-yang tile roof, bell and drum towers, wooden statues, and a bronze bell, and say the house serves the islanders and the trading ships that stopped to pray. The island visit fee is 70,000 VND per person from 10 June 2026. The 2026 city tourism list adds 20,000 VND for sanitation on the island.

figures.caption: The main hall at Hải Tạng, with the altar statues
figures.alt: Seated Buddha statues and offerings in the main hall of Hai Tang Pagoda

gettingThere: Land at Bai Lang and walk through the hamlet to Xóm Cấm. The pagoda is the landmark above Đồng Chùa.
The city page says the pagoda is about 20 km from the Hoi An shore. That distance is the crossing. The biodiversity agency says 18 km from Hoi An. Both stay.

legs.heading: From Bai Lang
legs.body: Walk from the landing through the hamlet to Xóm Cấm, above the fields called Đồng Chùa.

legs.heading: From Hoi An
legs.body: Boat from bến thủy nội địa Cửa Đại – Cù Lao Chàm to Bai Lang, then walk. The crossing is about 20 km on the city temple page and 18 km on the biodiversity agency page.

closed: No weekly closing day was printed. Check the gate on arrival.
